title: End-to-End Host Timing Model

model.evidence: MBBSEmu RTIHDLR implementation comments describe 18 Hz / ~55 ms real-time interval behavior and original DOS interrupt-level handling.
MBBSEmu MbbsHost main loop dispatches sessions, then ProcessRTKICK, ProcessRTIHDLR, ProcessSYSCYC, and ProcessTasks.
STTROU, STSROU, BEGIN_POLLING handling in MBBSEmu; _ljngame_sttrou/_ljngame_stsrou and _begin_polling strings in WCC/WBB MajorMUD DLLs.
RTKICK registers routines after N seconds in MBBSEmu; _rtkick/_my_rtkick in WCC/WBB DLLs.
ProcessSYSCYC in MBBSEmu host loop; _syscyc/_majormud_syscyc and background cadence bucket symbols in WCC/WBB DLLs.
WCC/WBB strings show autocombat, regen, background, delay, spawn-room delay, inactivity-round, and output strings.
model.state: Observed symbol presence; exact cadence unresolved

model.evidence: Host/session architecture implies modem/telnet latency affects observed output timing, not master gameplay cadence.

closed_assumptions: MajorMUD should not be modeled as owning an independent modern game loop.
The host/module API is the correct layer for tick investigation.
WCC and WBB MajorMUD DLL imports share the same timing-relevant symbol set in this pass.
open_gaps: Exact mapping of autocombat routines to host scheduler and delay values
Original-file provenance for 1500 ms MegaMUD CommandDelay/CombatPulse values
Whether 3-second global-message interval also governs regen/spell ticks
Output flush granularity in original Worldgroup host
